scope_note: ISSUES-axis spine for telegram-llm-bot, mined via the issue-surface lens (gaps users actually hit or demanded (GitHub issues, reaction-weighted)) from ['AstrBot', 'ChatGPT-Telegram-Bot', 'LangBot', 'nekro-agent']. Does NOT predict project-specific product direction — that is strategy, not completeness. Non-SCOPE axes are advisory in check.py until they beat the generic-baseline control.

required.what: Users need fast, reliable support for new LLM providers/models, custom endpoints, reasoning modes, embeddings, and model-list scanning without regressions.
required.day1_tell: Configure a newly released OpenAI-compatible model on a custom endpoint with reasoning enabled and embeddings listed, then scan/select the model list and complete one chat plus one embedding call without fallback or errors.

required.what: Users hit practical failures across Telegram, Feishu/Lark, WeCom, Discord, Minecraft and other adapters: message duplication, file/image send failures, long output failures, domain/config issues, and missing platform capabilities.
required.day1_tell: On each enabled adapter, send a long text, an image, and a file to a test chat and confirm delivery occurs once, succeeds, and long output is split rather than truncated or failed.

required.what: Users want safer and clearer control over tools, plugins, workflows, MCP servers, sandbox calls, permissions, disabled methods, and tool-call lifecycle behavior.
required.day1_tell: Disable one tool/plugin/MCP method, then ask the model to use it and confirm the UI/logs show it was blocked with a clear permission/lifecycle reason and no sandbox call executed.

required.what: Users expect robust upload, viewing, generation, transcription, summarization, and processing of images, files, audio, video, and YouTube-like content.
required.day1_tell: Upload an image, PDF, audio clip, video, and YouTube-style URL, then request summarize/transcribe/describe/generate actions and confirm each produces a usable result or clear supported-format error.

required.what: Users want reliable knowledge bases, vector storage, passive group history capture, memory initialization, summarization, timed resets, and safer persistence semantics.
required.day1_tell: Create a small knowledge base, add a document, query it in a new conversation, restart the service, and confirm retrieved context, memory initialization, history persistence, and reset behavior match configuration.

required.what: Users need practical group/channel administration: separate chat/tool permissions, admin-delegated commands, quotas, channel enable states, deletion, and manual human intervention.
required.day1_tell: As a delegated group admin, change chat permission, tool permission, quota, channel enable state, and delete one test item, then confirm unauthorized users cannot do the same.

required.what: Users raise concerns around audit findings, protocol/message spoofing, package validation, API auth fallback, sandbox exposure, and trusted/untrusted content boundaries.
required.day1_tell: Send spoofed protocol-like content, install an unsigned package/plugin, call the API without auth, and request sandbox access to secrets; confirm each is rejected or isolated with audit-visible logs.

required.what: Users struggle with Docker, proxies, local installs, Windows/Linux quirks, Android/WSL support, dependency imports, CPU requirements, working directories, and environment variables.
required.day1_tell: Fresh-install via the documented Docker/local path behind a proxy on the target OS, restart from a different working directory, and confirm dependencies, env vars, CPU compatibility, and startup all work.

required.what: Users want clearer UI state, dynamic waiting indicators, better error messages, debug-group reliability, login/autofill convenience, and less confusing frontend behavior.
required.day1_tell: Trigger a slow model response, a provider error, and a debug-group notification, then confirm the UI shows waiting state, actionable error text, reliable debug output, and no confusing stale state.

required.what: Users ask bots to initiate actions, run cron/wakeup flows, backup regularly, auto-update, send notifications, and act beyond passive chat.
required.day1_tell: Configure a cron/wakeup automation to run a backup and send a notification without user chat input, then confirm it executes on schedule, survives restart, and reports success/failure.
